newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel fall as China demand dwindles.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel fall as China demand dwindles.

text.p: The Singapore fuel oil and gas oil market closed weaker on Friday on poor Chinese demand and rising supplies, traders said.

Gas oil traded late day between a European major and a local trader for 150,000 barrels each for loading in Jan 25-29 at $31.65 a barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis, down slightly from Thursday's $31.70 traded level.

Traders said the weak market was primarily due to sharply lower Chinese demand for February cargoes and fears of large spot export availabilties from South Korea as all the new crude units start commercial production.

In addition, expectations for India's purchase of diesel in its supplementary February tender were cut to 150,000 barrels on Friday from 200,000 barrels on Thursday, offering a further bearish indication.
The gas oil swaps market fell sharply in reaction to the weak fundamentals with February last quoted at $29.90/$30.00 a barrel, down a hefty $1.00 from Thursday.
Fuel oil remained under selling pressure as the market was weighed down by ample supplies and poor Chinese demand.
February swaps was last quoted at $115.50/$116.50 per tonne, from Thursday's $117.00/$117.50, brokers said.
February fuel oil swaps traded at $116.00 and $115.75 a tonne, brokers said.
In the physical market, a major offered 20,000-tonne loading in February 3-7 at $118.00 per tonne, down $3 a tonne from Thursday's offer price.

The gasoline market was well supported by regional demand with a bid seen from a major for a 50,000 barrel 92-octane cargo for loading Jan 25-30 at $26.55 a barrel, 30 cents below Thursday's traded level.
An offer was seen for a 70,000-80,000 cargo at $26.00 a barrel but the quality was different from the major's bid.
